Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run-chase. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan stride out to open the innings for Pakistan. It will be Spencer Johnson to steam in with the ball for Australia. Here we go!
...THE RUN CHASE...

Pakistan did not begin well as they looked to bowl very full but once they started taking pace off, their bowlers became very useful. The likes of Afridi and Rauf were brilliant. Sufiyan Muqeem also impressed in the middle overs. Shaheen and Naseem came back well in the end. The bowlers will feel they have done their job can the batters do their job now? Australia on the other hand, will know this won't be an easy chase but they need to bowl well. An exciting second half awaits.

End of a fine bowling effort from Pakistan! The start though wasn't all that great! The hosts were off to a flier. They got to their fifty around the 3 over mark. Once the opening stand was broken, runs scoring got very tough and wickets also fell at regular intervals. A couple of batters got off to starts but none went on to make it big. They though will still feel they have a total which is just around par.
A bye to end then! A slower one down the leg side. Zampa moves across and looks to play the ramp shot but misses. They take one as the keeper fumbles.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Bang! Take that. Over the fence. What a start this is for the Aussies! On middle. Shorter. Short stands tall and pulls this one over the square leg fence. That's bread and butter for Short. He just loves that length. Pakistan under massive pressure here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Naseem Shah to Matthew Short, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Bang! That's 21 from the first over. Shaheen has been taken to the cleaners. Short and on middle. Jake stands tall and slams it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED AND FOUR! 15 from the over with a ball to go now! Shorter and around off. Jake Fraser-McGurk looks to pull. This flies off the top edge towards third man. Naseem Shah runs in. He looks to take it inches above the ground but spills it and it goes behind to the fence. How costly will this prove?
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Another juicy half volley. This is well outside off. This is lofted over the cover fielder and this goes to the fence too. This is a very expensive start from Afridi.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Shaheen continues to go full but finds no swing again. Jake Fraser-McGurk says thank you very much and lofts it down the ground and to the long on fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off. No swing again. This is driven to mid on. No swing on the first two balls, will Shaheen pull his length back?
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Straightaway the Aussies on the attack! Width on offer. This is well wide outside off. He looks to bring it back in but it doesn't. This is lofted over cover. It just stops before the ropes. Three taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Short, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the action to begin! Out walk the Pakistan players and they're followed by the Aussie openers, Jake Fraser-McGurk and Matthew Short.

Mohammad Rizwan, the Pakistan skipper says they showed great spirit in the first game. Adds they want to continue to show character. Mentions they have one change with Sufiyan Muqeem coming in for Haseebullah Khan.

Josh Inglis. the Australian skipper says he's happy to begin with a win. Adds he enjoyed the game despite it being a shorter one. Mentions they have a very good bowling attack and they are going unchanged for this contest.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan(C)(WK), Sahibzada Farhan, Usman Khan, Salman Agha, Irfan Khan, Abbas Afridi, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, Sufiyan Muqeem (in place of Haseebullah Khan).

Australia (Unchanged Playing XI) - Matthew Short, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Glenn Maxwell, Tim David, Marcus Stoinis, Josh Inglis(C)(WK), Aaron Hardie, Nathan Ellis, Xavier Bartlett, Spencer Johnson, Adam Zampa.
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and ELECTED TO BAT!

For Pakistan, this is a must-win game! They'll need to put in a better show than the last game. The specially their bowling which was quite all over the place. They'll be disappointed with their performance after the way they played in the ODIs. We surely expect a better outing from them in this one. Stay tuned for the toss and teams.

It is time for the second T20I and the action now moves to the SCG. The first one was quite a one-sided contest. It was a 7 over per side game which the Aussies dominated. They'll be looking to do the same in this one and seal the series with a game to go.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan now heads to Sydney for the second T20I of the three-match series between Australia and Pakistan. With Australia leading 1-0, the iconic Sydney Cricket Ground sets the stage for a high-stakes encounter as Mohammad Rizwan and his men aim to level the series and keep alive their hopes of a rare double white-ball series win down under. Lightning and thunder dominated much of the night in Brisbane during the first T20I, and it seemed unlikely that any play would be possible. However, a 7-over game was squeezed in just in time. After being sent into bat, fireworks from Glenn Maxwell powered Australia to 93, a target Pakistan found insurmountable. Despite the loss, the visitors won’t dwell too much on it, though they would admit that under the pressure applied by the Australian batters, the response from their pacers fell short of expectations. The defeat in Brisbane meant that Pakistan are still yet to secure their first T20I win against Australia on Australian soil. With an inexperienced batting lineup, Pakistan will rely heavily on the experience of Babar Azam and skipper Mohammad Rizwan if they are to push for a decider. Given Sydney’s history of aiding spinners as well, it will be interesting to see if Pakistan opt for a frontline spinner, potentially reshuffling their all-pace attack. For Australia, the win was a much-needed lift after a disappointing ODI series. Glenn Maxwell’s return to form was a significant positive but the opening pair of Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk had another subdued performance. On the bowling front, Nathan Ellis and Xavier Bartlett returned strongly after injury layoffs, delivering impactful performances that Australia will hope to build on as they aim to clinch the series at the SCG. In the 7-over shootout, Maxwell and David were promoted to number 3 and 4, respectively, while Inglis dropped himself to number 6. With a promising weather forecast in Sydney for the second T20I, which should allow a full game, the hosts are expected to revert to their regular batting order with Inglis likely to move back up to a higher position. All in all, it promises to be an exciting encounter in Sydney. Will Pakistan bounce back to force a series decider, or will Australia seal the series? We shall find out.
